en.html:
My words must have convinced her. Exactly opposite to the way she had desperately wanted.

A plain list of facts. No ornament, no complication. No room left to doubt.

The truth.
The truth she did not want.

Ichijou Ayane had asked the final question. Now this answer was hers to carry.

en.html:
Indigo flew toward us.

Deep, hard brilliance, with three pairs of legs and long feelers.

A longhorn beetle.

A tsurugi. Its enormous body and steel exoskeleton left no doubt on that point.

Dark armor beneath a rainy sky, but blending into the scenery was apparently beneath its dignity. It shone with an arrogant brilliance.

That luster seized the eyes. Looking was not optional. It declared one fact plainly:
A supreme-grade masterpiece.

Equal to Sengo Muramasa of Ise.
Perhaps greater.

en.html:
With that pronouncement, she turned and walked toward the gate.

Her small back receded beside the tsurugi. Then she stopped.

Looked back.

Our gazes met.

Rain and mist hid her eyes from me. From her side, what could she see? That I did not know.

She raised her right arm. Her index finger stood sharply out.

The nail's tip pointed precisely at my solar plexus.

　その足が、ふと止まった。

　振り返る。

　視線が絡む。

　雨靄に遮られ、俺に少女の瞳は窺えなかった。
　向こうからは――どうだろうか。

　一条が右腕を持ち上げる。
　人差し指を鋭く立てて。

　爪の先端が、俺の<ruby>鳩尾<rt>みぞおち</rt></ruby>を正確に指した。
